one_line: Real ~1 ha loss of sparse spinifex cover on a Gibson Desert dune crest, Nov 2024, leaving bright red sand; agent (small fire likeliest) not directly seen.
summary: before.png (Oct-Dec 2023 median) shows the footprint as unremarkable mottled red sandplain; after.png (Dec 2024-Jan 2025 median) shows a slightly brighter, smoother patch filling the box, and difference.png shows one isolated NE-SW blob of +0.02 to +0.04 brightness and about -0.03 NDVI with nothing comparable in the 1 km view. hires.png (Esri, picture dated 2025-08-02, after onset) shows a bare pale-sand patch about 100-130 m by 60-80 m with lobate soft edges and several surviving dark shrubs inside, sitting on a pale WNW-ESE dune-crest band, with no vehicle track, straight edge, spoil or structure anywhere in the 600 m view; wayback_strip.png shows the box vegetated like its surroundings in the 2014-2023 releases and bare only in the 2026 release. timeseries.png and the dossier series show inside brightness stepping about +0.03 above the ring after the onset and staying there to Sept 2026 (14 of 14 later scenes, Landsat shift 0.025 vs noise 0.003), while inside NBR keeps the same ~0.03 offset below the ring it had before, so no charred phase is recorded; two sceptics bracketed the onset to 2024-11-12..11-24 from individual scenes. The panel (3 of 3 refuting) concluded the detection is sound and the change is an ordinary loss of sparse vegetation exposing bright sand, but disagreed on the agent: two favoured a small self-extinguishing spinifex fire in the November storm season (MODIS 500 m/1 km products cannot see a ~1 ha burn), one favoured mechanical scraping or aeolian stripping. Because no hotspot, char, track or blade mark was observed, the cause is likely but not shown, so the verdict is probably ordinary rather than explained.
explanation: Loss of roughly 0.6-1.9 ha of sparse spinifex and shrub cover on a linear-dune crest inside the Gibson Desert Nature Reserve between 2024-11-12 and 2024-11-24, exposing bright red sand that has stayed bare since (d_brightness +0.037, d_swir +0.114, d_ndvi -0.032; hires.png and wayback_strip.png show the vegetation gone). Most plausibly a small, self-extinguishing spinifex fire during the November dry-storm season, in a landscape that context.png shows to be a fire-scar mosaic; mechanical clearing is disfavoured by the lobate edges and the absence of any track or straight edge at 1 m, and wind stripping by the 12-day onset and the centroid fixed to within 10 m for 20 months. The ignition or agent itself was not captured in any available image.
next_step: A VIIRS 375 m active-fire lookup (VNP14IMG / VJ114IMG via FIRMS with a map key) for -24.678, 126.144 between 2024-11-12 and 2024-11-24: a hotspot would confirm a small fire outright. Failing that, any Planet or Maxar scene from 13-25 Nov 2024 showing a charred/ash-grey patch versus blade marks or vehicle tracks at the footprint, or the WA DBCA fire-history and DMIRS Program-of-Work records for the reserve in November 2024.
